subject: Service backstop & monthly offset proposal — AcmeTech migration window
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel@acmetech.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmetech.com, legal@acmetech.com
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary service backstop + monthly offset during EU migration

Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re targeting an EU network migration the week of Sep 13 and expect a short period of elevated risk to reach traffic parity across our new edge providers. AcmeTech needs a written exception from standard global uptime language for a 3-month window in the EU region (Sep–Nov).

Specifically, we propose:
- Temporary commitment of 99.80% for EU region (instead of standard 99.95%) for the 3-month window
- A fixed monthly offset (service credit) of $7,500 capped per month if uptime falls below 99.80% during that window
- One-time onboarding credit of $10,000 if we sign by Aug 15 to help cover migration testing costs

We prefer a dollar-offset so our finance team can reconcile to the PO. I attached our migration plan so you can see the dates and risk windows. If Redwood can accept this structure, please confirm next steps (procurement path, PO, contract language). If you prefer an alternate formulation (service credits vs dollars, pro-rata calculation), say so and we can iterate.

Thanks —
Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Infrastructure
AcmeTech

Attachments: acmetech-migration-plan.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Daniel Park <daniel@acmetech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary service backstop + monthly offset during EU migration

Daniel —

Appreciate the clear proposal and the migration plan — helpful context. Looping in Laura (legal/contracts) and Ben (pricing/offer) to weigh in. A few quick notes from the Redwood side:

- We can consider a temporary regional carveout, but we need to preserve our global SLO accounting and avoid billing complexity that could cascade across enterprise invoicing.
- Two options we typically offer: (A) monetary offset (your proposed fixed monthly dollar credit) with a clear cap and pro-rata calculation, or (B) compute/service credits (e.g., reserved-hour offset) to simplify invoicing.
- For a 3-month window we’d like to include: an explicit start/end date window, telemetry acceptance criteria (how Acme will report incidents), and a single point of contact for breach/dispute.

To move forward I suggest Redwood proposes a precise formula so procurement can accept language and we can produce a clean amendment. My rough counterproposal below — let me know which approach you prefer (dollars v service credits):

Counterproposal (monetary):
- Temporary EU uptime commitment: 99.80% for 2026-09-13T00:00:00Z to 2026-11-30T23:59:59Z
- Monthly offset: 30% of one monthly committed invoice, capped at $6,000/month (cap lowers financial unpredictability while acknowledging migration risk)
- Onboarding credit: one-time $8,000 applied to first invoice after the migration window if contract amendment signed by 2026-08-15
- Telemetry: Acme provides incident window reports and we’ll reconcile offsets within 30 days of monthly close

If Acme prefers service credits instead of dollars, we can offer: 200 reserved GPU-hours credit (valued against standard list price) per month capped at equivalent of $7,500.

Laura/Ben — can you review the legal/financial implications? If this shape is acceptable, I’ll draft the amendment language and a DocuSign packet and route to procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0142

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Daniel Park <daniel@acmetech.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-03T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary service backstop + monthly offset during EU migration

Daniel / Marissa —

Thanks for the clear ask. From a contract standpoint, a temporary regional carveout is workable if we: (1) limit scope to the EU region and the exact dates; (2) add explicit telemetry & reconciliation language; and (3) keep the remedy capped and non-duplicative with other credits. A few edits to Marissa’s counterproposal I recommend:

1) Monthly offset calculation: use a pro-rata formula tied to measured downtime minutes in the EU region, not a flat percent-of-invoice. Example language we prefer: "Monthly Offset = min(cap, (DowntimeMinutes / MinutesInMonth) * MonthlyCommitmentUSD)". Cap = $6,000. This makes offsets proportional and defensible in audits.

2) Onboarding credit: prefer this as a one-time invoice credit (applied against first month) conditioned on signatures by Aug 15. Keep $8,000.

3) Telemetry & dispute: Acme to provide incident timeline + raw traceroute/edge logs where applicable; Redwood will produce aggregated uptime report. Disputes escalate to a 3-business-day review cadence with one neutral audit window (shared S3 link).

4) Termination/rollback: If migration extends beyond Nov 30, carveout can be extended only by mutual written agreement and the offset cap steps up 20% per month of extension (to reflect prolonged operational risk).

I’ll attach a short amendment draft and redline to the standard SLA template for your procurement/legal to review. Ben — note the cap and the extension step-up impact revenue recognition; flagging for your team’s review.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla-exception-draft.docx

From: Daniel Park <daniel@acmetech.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmetech.com, legal@acmetech.com
Date: 2026-08-04T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary service backstop + monthly offset during EU migration

Laura/Marissa —

Thanks — that all looks reasonable. We prefer the pro-rata formula Laura suggested (makes more sense for our audit team). Confirming Acme agrees to the $6,000 cap and the onboarding $8,000 credit conditioned on signature by Aug 15. We also accept the extension-by-agreement language and the 20% step-up on the cap if the window is extended.

Next steps from our side: procurement will prepare a PO (ref ACME-PO-9987) and legal will review your attached draft; we expect to push the PO by Aug 10 if the amendment language is final. Please go ahead and put the amendment into a DocuSign packet and route to legal@acmetech.com and procurement@acmetech.com.

Looking forward —
Daniel
